goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? issues a live SQL query on every call instead of using a cached in-memory check, adding DB load and latency to high-traffic public embed endpoints

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (a DB query) every time it is invoked. The embed access checks were changed to call this method (e.g., `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`), meaning each public embed request now performs at least one SQL lookup instead of the prior in-memory `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` string check. No caching layer is added here, so the stated DB load/latency impact is a verifiable regression in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: host_allowed? uses record_for_host(host).present? which instantiates a full AR record when exists? would suffice for the boolean existence check

adjudication.rationale: `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` is implemented as `record_for_host(host).present?`, and `record_for_host` does `where(...).first`, which indeed instantiates an ActiveRecord object when a match exists. Using `exists?` could be a minor performance optimization, but the current behavior is correct and verifiably works as a boolean check. This is not a bug/security/correctness issue introduced by the diff, just a micro-optimization suggestion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts un-sanitized host values (with schemes/paths) that will never match at lookup time, silently breaking embeddable-host authorization after upgrade
Migration builds SQL via unescaped string interpolation of host values, which can raise a SQL error and block the upgrade entirely

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration inserts each host using raw string interpolation into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ... )"`. `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` (split by newlines) and is not escaped/quoted via the DB adapter. If any host line contains a single quote or other SQL-significant characters, the INSERT can fail with a SQL syntax error and halt the migration/upgrade. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host lookup is case-sensitive against a lower(host) query, breaking matching for mixed-case referers
record_for_host lookup is port-sensitive: validation allows stored hosts with ports but uri.host strips the port, so port-qualified hosts never match

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost` allows saving hosts with ports: the validation regex permits `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the `before_validation` cleanup strips protocol and path but does not remove a `:port`, so values like `example.com:8080` can be persisted. However `record_for_host` does `uri = URI(host)` then `host = uri.host`, which drops the port (Ruby `URI#host` returns only the hostname). It then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so a stored `example.com:8080` will never match a referer like `http://example.com:8080/...` (it will look for `example.com`). This makes port-qualified whitelist entries ineffective.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client delete() in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch on destroyRecord(), leaving unhandled promise rejections with no user feedback

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete() action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` but does not attach a `.catch(...)` handler. If the DELETE request fails (network/server error, validation, 403, etc.), the promise rejection is not handled in this code path and there is no user-visible error feedback (unlike save(), which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded in store.js.es6 crashes on null id-lists and can produce undefined entries for unknown ids

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch triggers when a key matches `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` and `m[2]` is truthy, then does `obj[k].map(...)`. If the server sends a `*_ids` field as `null` (or anything non-array), this will throw because `null`/non-array has no `.map`. Also, unlike the singular `*_id` branch which only assigns when `hydrated` is truthy, the plural branch assigns the raw `map` result without filtering, so any missing lookup (`_lookupSubType` returning `undefined`/`null`) will produce `undefined` entries in the resulting array. Both behaviors are directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration copies legacy embeddable_hosts values raw, including http://-prefixed values that record_for_host can never match, silently breaking embedding for existing sites; no migration test covers the data migration path

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` inserts each legacy line `h` into `embeddable_hosts.host` via raw SQL (`INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) which bypasses the model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http://`, `https://`, and paths. Later, host checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` which parses the URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If a migrated row is stored as `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`, `uri.host` will be `eviltrout.com` / `example.com` and will not match the raw stored value, causing `host_allowed?` to return false and breaking embedding for those existing configurations. The diff also adds no spec covering this data-migration behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates untrusted legacy setting strings directly into SQL without escaping, so a host value containing a quote breaks the migration; untested with hostile/odd values

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration reads the legacy site_settings value for 'embeddable_hosts', splits it into lines, then runs raw SQL like:

execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"

Because `h` is interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL string without escaping/quoting via bind parameters, any host value containing a single quote (or other SQL-special characters) will break the migration (syntax error) and could be leveraged for SQL injection if the site_settings row was tampered with. This is a verifiable correctness/security issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was replaced to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (host + category), while a new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)` and related category fabricators that previously lived in `category_fabricator.rb`. That is a verifiable swap/misnaming of fabricator file contents introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs are vacuous (only assert class inheritance) with no coverage of save_host category_id defaulting, validation failure path, update/destroy with nonexistent id causing NoMethodError 500, or EmbeddingController#update no-op

adjudication.rationale: The new controller specs in `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only assert the controller inherits from `Admin::AdminController`, providing no behavioral coverage. Additionally, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy` do `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without handling `host == nil`, which would raise a `NoMethodError` (500) for nonexistent IDs. `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` also performs no update logic and just re-renders the serializer, so the note that it’s a no-op is accurate from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host downcases the stored column but not the incoming URI host, so mixed-case referers like http://EvilTrout.com fail host_allowed?; also hosts saved with a port can never match since uri.host strips the port; both edge cases untested

adjudication.rationale:
The port-related part is a real correctness issue in the diff: `EmbeddableHost` allows storing hosts with a port (validation permits `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` and `before_validation` does not strip ports), but `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and uses `uri.host` (which excludes the port) and then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That can never match a stored value like `example.com:3000`, so `host_allowed?` will incorrectly reject referers when the DB entry includes a port. This edge case is not covered by the added specs.

The mixed-case referer claim is less clearly a bug because Ruby's `URI(...).host` is typically normalized to lowercase during parsing, so the lack of explicit downcasing may not cause failures in practice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import category behavior change only tested on the happy path: no test for no matching host yielding category nil, and no test for multiple hosts with different categories selecting the correct per-host category

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `TopicEmbed.import` to set `category: eh.try(:category_id)` based on `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and adds a spec asserting the category matches for a single fabricated host. It’s true there is no added test for (a) no matching host (eh=nil) or (b) multiple hosts with different categories. However, that’s a test coverage gap rather than a verifiable defect/bug introduced by the code in this diff; the code path itself behaves deterministically (category nil when no host match, host-based lookup when matched).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that just re-serializes without changing anything, yet the client calls embedding.update({}) from saveChanges; no test exercises PUT to reveal the broken save

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` does not read any params or modify state; it simply re-renders the same serialized `@embedding` as `show`. On the client, `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would issue a PUT (routes include `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`). As written, that PUT cannot persist anything and will appear to “save” while changing nothing. The added specs for `Admin::EmbeddingController` do not exercise PUT/update behavior, so this would not be caught by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No JavaScript test coverage for the new admin UI, and EmbeddingSerializer uses has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids so the show payload lacks the embedded records the store's _hydrateEmbedded needs, likely rendering an empty hosts table

adjudication.rationale: The “no JavaScript test coverage” portion is a general process concern, not a concrete defect introduced by the diff. The second claim misreads how `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` works in this codebase: the diff explicitly updates the client store `_hydrateEmbedded` to handle `*_ids` arrays (e.g., `embeddable_host_ids`) by populating the plural association (`embeddable_hosts`). With `embed: :ids`, Discourse serializers typically sideload the associated records alongside the `*_ids` list, which is exactly what `_lookupSubType` expects; nothing in the diff indicates the records would be missing from the payload, so an “empty hosts table” is not verifiable from this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test in topic_spec is vacuous since embed_truncate defaults to false, and the production code dropped the embeddable-hosts condition entirely — an untested behavioral change making first posts expandable whenever embed_truncate is on

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, so the “embeddable_hosts condition dropped” part is verifiable. However, the proposed finding overstates the behavior: first posts are not expandable merely when `embed_truncate` is on; they still require `has_topic_embed?`. Also, the claim about a specific vacuous test in `topic_spec` (“is false if embeddable_host is blank”) is not verifiable from the provided diff (the `expandable_first_post?` spec section is truncated and no such test is shown). Given the migration from a site setting to the `EmbeddableHost` model, removing the old site-setting presence check is plausibly intentional rather than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store _hydrateEmbedded plural path throws on null/absent *_ids (obj[k].map) and hydrated || [] is dead code; new store tests only cover well-formed arrays

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch runs when a key matches `/(.+)_id(s?)$/` and `m[2]` is truthy (i.e., `*_ids`). It does `obj[k].map(...)` without checking that `obj[k]` is an array. If the payload contains `something_ids: null` (or any non-array), this will throw at runtime (`Cannot read property 'map' of null`). The previous singular logic didn’t have this kind of immediate failure mode. Also, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead because `map` always returns an array when it runs; it won’t return `null/undefined` (and if `obj[k]` is null, it throws before reaching the `|| []`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller_spec 'missing host' test now relies on ambient DB state (no embeddable_hosts rows) instead of explicitly stating its precondition as it did with SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil
Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category site setting was never set, because execute(...)[0] returns nil and nil['id'] is called before the category_id == 0 fallback
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: the migration assumes execute(...)[0] exists and immediately indexes into ['id'], which crashes when no rows are returned (embed_category never set). This matches the golden comment’s missing nil/empty-result check leading to a crash and broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts old embeddable_hosts values verbatim (e.g. http://eviltrout.com) bypassing before_validation stripping, so stored hosts never match record_for_host and embedding silently stops working after upgrade
matched_golden_ids: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that the migration copies embeddable_hosts values verbatim via raw SQL, bypassing the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization/stripping (e.g., removing http(s):// and paths). As a result, the new host lookup comparing only the bare host may not match migrated rows, breaking existing embedding configs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration has no uniqueness check, allowing duplicate embeddable_hosts rows to be created

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates the `embeddable_hosts` table without any unique index/constraint on `host`, and it bulk-inserts rows from the old `site_settings` value by splitting on newlines and running raw `INSERT` statements with no de-duplication. If the old setting contains duplicate hosts (or host variants that later normalize to the same host), multiple rows can be created for the same host. The model also lacks a `validates_uniqueness_of` on `host`, so duplicates remain possible beyond the migration. This can cause ambiguous behavior since `record_for_host` uses `.first` on matching rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the various `:category` fabricators, so the finding is factually accurate about the swap. However, this is not clearly a functional/correctness defect by itself: Fabrication typically loads all files under `spec/fabricators/**`, and fabricator definitions are keyed by the symbol (`:category`, `:embeddable_host`), not by filename. With both files still present and presumably loaded, `Fabricate(:category)` and `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` will still work. The issue is primarily organizational/confusing rather than a verifiable bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingSerializer uses embed: :ids so the client cannot hydrate embeddable_host records, resulting in an array of undefined and a broken admin embedding page; should use embed: :objects
EmbeddableHostsController#update crashes with 500 when the record is missing because save_host(nil) calls host.host= on nil

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If no record exists for that id, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...` and `host.category_id = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil` and result in a 500. There is no guard or 404 handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController#destroy crashes with 500 when the record is missing (e.g. double-click delete, stale tab) because host.destroy is called on nil

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb#destroy, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy`. If no record matches (e.g., stale tab, double delete, already-deleted record), `host` will be nil and `nil.destroy` will raise a NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a controlled 404/success response. There is no nil check or `find_by!`/`render_not_found` handling in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: save_host accesses params[:embeddable_host][:host] without a guard, so a malformed request body causes a 500 instead of a 400/validation error

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host, the code unconditionally dereferences nested params: `host.host = params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If the request omits `embeddable_host` (or it is not a Hash), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be nil and `[:host]` will raise (e.g., `NoMethodError: undefined method '[]' for nil:NilClass`), resulting in a 500 rather than a controlled 400/validation-style error. There is no guard or use of `fetch`/strong params in the diff to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hosts saved with a port suffix (e.g. example.com:8080) pass validation but can never match in record_for_host since uri.host excludes the port; port should be stripped or compared

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost` allows and preserves a port in `host` (regex `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but not `:port`). But `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. `uri.host` excludes the port, so a stored record like `example.com:8080` will never match a referer `http://example.com:8080/...` (it will look for `example.com`). Therefore such saved hosts can pass validation but will never be considered allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Store plural hydration unconditionally deletes *_ids keys and replaces them with arrays of undefined when the sub-type can't be resolved, potentially corrupting unrelated payloads; also hydrated || [] is dead code since map never returns falsy

adjudication.rationale: In store.js `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch matches keys ending in `_ids` and always does `delete obj[k]` after `map`, regardless of whether `_lookupSubType` can resolve any of the referenced records. If the referenced objects aren’t present in `root`, `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined`/`null`, producing an array of unresolved values and removing the original ids array entirely (unlike the singular `_id` case, which only deletes the key when hydration succeeds). Also, `hydrated || []` is indeed dead because `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op and the client saveChanges() path is unreachable dead code; the fake OpenStruct embedding model exists only to satisfy the REST adapter shape

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders the serialized `@embedding` OpenStruct and does not persist anything (no params read, no DB writes). On the client, `admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, but the new `embedding.hbs` template provides no UI element/action that triggers `saveChanges` (only `addHost` and per-host save/delete inside the `embeddable-host` component). Additionally, `fetch_embedding` constructs an `OpenStruct` with a fixed `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts`, indicating it is a synthetic model to satisfy the REST/Ember store shape rather than a real persisted resource. Together, this makes the PUT route/action effectively a no-op and the client saveChanges path unused in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_spec.rb 'embeddable_host is blank' test is now vacuous since expandable_first_post? no longer consults embeddable hosts, misleading maintainers about actual gating logic

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Topic#expandable_first_post?` to no longer consult `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` (it now only checks `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`). However, the provided diff excerpt for `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` is truncated right after the start of the `describe "expandable_first_post?"` block, so it does not show any existing test asserting behavior when “embeddable_host(s) is blank”, nor whether such a test remains and is now vacuous/misleading. Without seeing that test still present and structured in a way that would pass vacuously, the finding isn’t verifiable from the diff shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostSerializer's id, host, and category_id methods are redundant dead weight, duplicating default ApplicationSerializer attribute behavior

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbeddableHostSerializer` declares `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` and then defines methods `id`, `host`, and `category_id` that simply return `object.id`, `object.host`, and `object.category_id`. This is redundant, but it does not introduce a bug, security issue, or correctness defect—Rails/ActiveModel serializers commonly allow either implicit attribute accessors or explicit methods, and the explicit methods here do not change behavior. This is a style/cleanup suggestion rather than a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Component delete action lacks .catch(popupAjaxError) on destroyRecord, so server-side destroy failures give the user no feedback and the row silently remains

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` but does not attach a `.catch(...)`. Unlike `save()`, which does `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, a failed server-side destroy (4xx/5xx/network) will reject the promise and no user-facing error handler in this component will run; the row also won’t be removed because `deleteHost` is only sent in the `then` branch. This matches the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category site setting has no matching row (nil deref on [0]['id'] lookup), also affects uncategorized_category_id at line 18

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for the `embed_category` lookup. If that SELECT returns zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` is unset/blank, or its value doesn’t match any category name), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError` before `.to_i` runs. Similarly, the fallback `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` will also crash if that setting row is missing. These nil-derefs are verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Join on s.value = c.name is fragile — the old setting likely stored a category id, not a name, so the lookup silently fails or crashes

Backfill inserts raw host values without normalization; hosts stored as 'http://eviltrout.com' or with path suffixes will never match record_for_host's bare-hostname comparison, breaking previously-working embeds

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the migration backfills `embeddable_hosts` via raw SQL inserts (`execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`), which bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. After migration, rows may contain values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (previously allowed by `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`). But `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the referer/embed URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, i.e., against the bare hostname (`discourse.org`, `example.com`). Those raw backfilled rows won’t match, breaking embeds that previously worked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Destructive DELETE FROM site_settings with no down/rollback path; a failed deploy and re-run silently produces an empty hosts table, losing all embeddable host configuration

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `change` with raw `execute` statements including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` and is not wrapped in a `reversible`/`up`/`down` block, making it irreversible (no rollback path to restore the deleted settings). Additionally, it uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, so if the migration were to fail before being recorded in `schema_migrations` and then be re-run, the table would be dropped/recreated; since the source `site_settings` rows may already have been deleted, the re-run would not be able to re-seed hosts, potentially resulting in an empty `embeddable_hosts` table and lost configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table with force: true drops the table if it already exists, compounding the re-run data-loss hazard

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the diff adds `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the existing table before creating it (if it exists), which can destroy any existing data and also masks the safer failure you’d get if the table already exists. That is a concrete, verifiable behavior introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unescaped interpolation of free-text setting values into raw SQL; a stored value containing a single quote causes a syntax error aborting the migration or inserts malformed data (also an admin-only injection vector)
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same core problem: values are being interpolated directly into raw SQL without escaping/parameterization, which can break SQL syntax (e.g., single quotes) and enables SQL injection. The candidate even explicitly mentions it as an injection vector, aligning with the golden recommendation to use parameter binding/proper quoting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host compares case-sensitively: URI#host does not downcase but the query applies lower(host), so mixed-case referers like http://EvilTrout.com fail the lookup
destroy action calls nil.destroy when the record doesn't exist, returning 500 instead of 404; update has the same nil-host hole causing NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record exists, `host` will be `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)`, and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...`, which will raise `NoMethodError` on `nil`. `destroy` calls `host.destroy` unconditionally, also raising on `nil`. There is no guard or `render_not_found`, so this would result in a 500 rather than a 404 for missing IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting was never set, because execute returns empty result and [0]['id'] is called on nil; the if category_id == 0 fallback is unreachable dead code

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, `category_id = execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` assumes the SQL returns at least one row. If the `site_settings` row for `embed_category` does not exist (or doesn’t join to any category), `execute(...)` yields an empty result, so `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError` before `.to_i` runs. That means the subsequent fallback `if category_id == 0` cannot be reached in that case (it only runs if the first line succeeded and produced 0).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates host values unescaped into SQL, causing SQL injection or breakage on hosts containing quotes/special characters

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, where `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` value (`embeddable_hosts`). If any host line contains a single quote or other SQL-significant characters, the INSERT will break; and because it is unescaped interpolation into SQL, a crafted value could alter the SQL being executed. This is a real correctness/security issue introduced by the diff; it should use proper quoting/parameterization (e.g., `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration copies prefixed host entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' verbatim into embeddable_hosts.host, but record_for_host compares against uri.host, so existing hosts silently stop matching and embedding returns 403 after upgrade

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, existing `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` lines are inserted via raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This bypasses the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If a migrated row contains `http://eviltrout.com` or `https://example.com/1234`, it will not equal `eviltrout.com` / `example.com`, so `host_allowed?` returns false and embedding requests will be rejected (403/InvalidAccess) after upgrade for those entries. The diff even shows tests fabricating hosts with schemes/paths, which would work through callbacks, but the migration path would not normalize them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingSerializer uses embed: :ids without side-loading host objects, so the client store's _hydrateEmbedded resolves embeddable_host_ids to an array of nils, rendering blank rows on the admin page

Admin::EmbeddingController#update re-serializes and returns success without persisting anything, and the client sends an empty payload to a likely mismatched URL, giving a silent-pass save that never surfaces errors

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not modify any persisted state; it simply re-renders `@embedding`, which is built in `fetch_embedding` as an `OpenStruct` containing `EmbeddableHost.all`. On the client side, `admin-embedding` controller’s `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` with an empty payload, so even if the server expected changes, none are sent, and the response will look like a successful save regardless. However, the URL is not “mismatched”: the JS adapter returns `/admin/customize/embedding`, which matches the added Rails `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host never matches stored hosts with ports (e.g. example.com:8080) since uri.host excludes the port, while a referer with a port matches a portless stored host, making port handling asymmetric

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, stored hosts can include a port because the validation regex allows an optional ":port" and the before_validation normalization strips scheme/path but does not remove a port. However record_for_host(host) parses the input with URI() and then uses `uri.host`, which excludes the port, and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. As a result, a stored value like `example.com:8080` will never match (`uri.host` => `example.com`). Conversely, an incoming referer `http://example.com:8080/...` will also yield `uri.host` => `example.com`, so it will match a portless stored entry, making port handling asymmetric and preventing port-specific allowlisting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host does not downcase uri.host before lower(host) = ?, so referers with uppercase characters fail to match stored lowercase hosts
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: the SQL compares lower(host) to a parameter that is not lowercased/normalized, so mixed- or uppercase referer hosts may not match even though the intent is case-insensitive matching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Global store hydration change deletes and rewrites every *_ids key for all rest models, replacing raw ids with possibly nil entries when lookup fails, breaking existing consumers reading obj.some_ids; the hydrated || [] fallback is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `_hydrateEmbedded` was broadened from matching only `*_id` to matching `*_id` and `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`. For any key ending in `_ids`, it now unconditionally maps the id array through `_lookupSubType` and then **deletes the original `obj[k]`** (`delete obj[k]`). This means payloads that previously exposed raw `some_ids` arrays will now lose that field and instead get `obj[pluralize(subType)]` containing the lookup results, which may include `undefined`/`null` elements when `_lookupSubType` can’t resolve an id (there is no filtering). Also, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead code because `map(...)` always returns an array (truthy), so the fallback won’t run. This is a real, verifiable behavior change that can break consumers expecting `*_ids` to remain as ids.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update and #destroy raise NoMethodError (500) on a nonexistent/stale id instead of returning 404
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that update/destroy fetch an EmbeddableHost by id without handling the not-found case, leading to calling methods on nil and raising a NoMethodError (500) instead of responding with 404.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost before_validation calls self.host.sub! which raises NoMethodError when host is nil, producing a 500 instead of a validation error

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, the `before_validation` block unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., missing/blank `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create/update, or any code path building a record without `host`), `nil.sub!` will raise `NoMethodError` during validation, resulting in a 500 rather than a normal validation error. The `validates_format_of :host` does not prevent this because it runs after `before_validation`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The topic spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' has no before block and passes regardless of the host check, making it a vacuous regression test

adjudication.rationale: The diff snippet for `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` is truncated right after the start of `describe "expandable_first_post?" do` and only shows removed lines (`let(:topic)` and the start of a `before do`). It does not include any example named “is false if embeddable_host is blank”, nor does it show the full structure of the specs in that block. Because the claimed test and its missing `before` block are not visible/verifiable in the provided diff, the finding cannot be confirmed as a real problem introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents are swapped: category fabricators live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb and vice versa, so filenames lie about contents

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines category-related fabricators; it now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`. Meanwhile the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the category, diff_category, happy_category, and private_category fabricators that previously lived in `category_fabricator.rb`. So the filenames/content are effectively swapped, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embeddable-host component's destroyRecord().then(...) lacks a .catch(popupAjaxError), so failed deletions silently leave the row in the UI with no feedback

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); }); without any .catch(...) handler. If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and the UI provides no error feedback and does not remove the host from the list (since removal only happens in the then). This matches the finding: failed deletions would appear to do nothing and give no popupAjaxError feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host validation regex caps TLDs at [a-z]{2,5} and requires a dot+TLD, rejecting valid hosts like .museum, future gTLDs, localhost, and single-label intranet names that the old setting accepted

adjudication.rationale: The new model `EmbeddableHost` introduces `validates_format_of :host, with: /\A[a-z0-9]+([\-\.]{1}[a-z0-9]+)*\.[a-z]{2,5}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(\/.*)?\Z/i`, which (1) requires at least one dot + TLD and (2) limits the TLD to 2–5 letters. This will reject valid real-world domains with longer TLDs (e.g. `.museum`) and any future/modern gTLDs longer than 5 chars, and it will also reject hosts like `localhost` or single-label intranet hostnames. The previous SiteSetting-based allowlist logic compared the parsed referer host to configured entries and could accept `localhost`/single-label hosts (e.g. `embeddable_hosts = 'localhost'` would match referer host `localhost`). So this is a concrete behavioral regression introduced by the diff.
